headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: broad-egress support agent can expose shared project data while the audio-speech hub lacks isolation and write surfaces are undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is an open-source AI-engineering hub with MCP/RAG tags, while agent B uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and can run browsers. A shared filesystem or message bridge is not explicitly documented, but B’s tool-rich runtime could ingest A-produced content if connected. Uncertainty about the bridge escalates this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected through a shared MCP server, clipboard, or workspace, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF B parses A-generated files or web content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer B.
mitigations: Disable shared MCPs between the agents for the session.
Route A outputs through a plain-text review step before B consumes them.
Restrict B to allowlisted tools only for this workflow.
Use separate workspaces for A and B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, session history, and provider auth data, and has broad network egress. A has no documented isolation or data-class limits beyond no network egress. If they share a workspace, B can exfiltrate A-related files or secrets to third parties; the lack of a documented barrier makes this dangerous by default.
conditions: IF A and B share any filesystem or synced workspace, B can read A-produced artifacts.
IF B is allowed to send context to external APIs, shared files may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different OS users.
Remove shared workspace mounts for the run.
Disable B network egress for this task.
Redact secrets from AGENTS.md and provider auth prompts before B runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has broad egress, browser, subprocess, and multiple-instance support; A’s write surfaces are undocumented, so a direct write-write collision is not proven. However, B’s file access plus runtime-injected tools can conflict with any shared mutable workspace if A also writes there. Because A’s mutability is unknown, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, file races can occur.
IF B runs multiple instances against shared state, edits may overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Serialize edits through one agent at a time.
Disable multi-instance execution for B.
Use git branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B exposes team_send_message and task creation APIs, so it can act on upstream content. A is an AI-engineering hub likely to emit generated guidance or artifacts, but no direct verification loop is documented. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions; the interaction is plausible in default agent workflows.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated instructions without verification, incorrect steps can propagate.
IF B uses team_send_message or task creation based on A output, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output.
Add a verification checklist between A and B.
Limit B to read-only summarization of A output.
Log and diff A outputs before execution.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on A-to-B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles provider authentication data, installation identifiers, session history, and project code, while A’s compliance posture is undocumented. If the pair processes regulated or sensitive project data, retention and residency mismatches are plausible. A is not cited for a specific jurisdiction, so only B’s documented data handling is relevant here.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s session history or provider auth prompts, retention obligations may be triggered.
IF A and B have different retention or residency defaults, compliance gaps can arise.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into B prompts.
Clear B session history after the task.
Review B’s retention settings before use.
Store secrets outside agent-visible files.
requires-engineering: document a data-class handling policy for the pair.
